studies.Study: Grieb SM et al. (2009) [PMID: 19328261] — estimate 1 · Mixed
studies.Reference: Food groups and renal cell carcinoma: results from a case-control study.
studies.Title: Food groups and renal cell carcinoma: results from a case-control study.
studies.Authors: Grieb SM, Theis RP, Burr D, Benardot D, Siddiqui T, Asal NR
studies.Journal: Journal of the American Dietetic Association
studies.Population: Incident renal cell carcinoma cases from hospital records and the Florida cancer registry with population controls identified through random-digit dialing

sample_size.excerpt: Incident cases (n=335) were identified from hospital records and the Florida cancer registry, and population controls (n=337) frequency matched by age (+/-5 years), sex, and race were identified through random-digit dialing.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 335 + 337 = 672

cases.excerpt: Incident cases (n=335) were identified from hospital records and the Florida cancer registry, and population controls (n=337) frequency matched by age (+/-5 years), sex, and race were identified through random-digit dialing.

effect_size.excerpt: Tomato consumption decreased renal cell carcinoma risk for the total population and for men (all subjects: OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.31, 0.81; men: OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.24, 0.95).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Tomato consumption decreased renal cell carcinoma risk for the total population and for men (all subjects: OR 0.50, 95% CI 0.31, 0.81; men: OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.24, 0.95).

comparison.excerpt: Tomato consumption decreased renal cell carcinoma risk for the total population and for men

design.excerpt: A case-control study was conducted from 2003-2006.

timing.excerpt: A case-control study was conducted from 2003-2006.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Eating habits were assessed through the use of the 70-item Block food frequency questionnaire.

gender.excerpt: frequency matched by age (+/-5 years), sex, and race
